issues.suggestedFix: Replace the URL with https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/extensions/dependency-injection/guidelines. Re-check that the page text actually covers captive dependencies and ValidateScopes/ValidateOnBuild. If it does not, cite the page that does.

issues.claim: In Development the default host turns on scope validation, and the app fails at startup with an error like "Cannot consume scoped service ... from singleton ...".
issues.problem: The default Development host enables both ValidateScopes and ValidateOnBuild. Failing at startup, inside builder.Build(), comes from ValidateOnBuild. Scope validation alone would fail on first resolution, which is what the stub's answerHinge says. The explanation credits only scope validation. The RU text has the same flaw.
issues.suggestedFix: Write: "In Development the default host enables ValidateScopes and ValidateOnBuild, so builder.Build() throws an InvalidOperationException (\"Error while validating the service descriptor ... Cannot consume scoped service 'ShopDbContext' from singleton 'IPriceCache'\")." Mirror this in locales.ru.explanation.

issues.claim: bugLineSets: [[5], [20]] and "Selecting either of these two lines is accepted"
issues.problem: A candidate who understands the whole lifetime mismatch and selects both lines 5 and 20 would be marked wrong. The answer text says either line is accepted, but the validator treats [5,20] as a different selection.
The Development-only default for ValidateOnBuild/ValidateScopes depends on the host version (WebApplicationBuilder, .NET 6+), and the guide asks for dotnetVersion in that case.

The excerpt supports only the class-based middleware shape (RequestDelegate constructor, InvokeAsync). It says nothing about headers after next() or HasStarted. The key claim is supported only by the best-practices page.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link as a reference for the middleware class shape, or swap it for the middleware overview page. Do not use it to back the header claim.
